title: Pixelbolt fluid effects
description: Start fire, smoke, explosions and splashes from a preset (pixel_help topic presets, then pixel_compile with preset); for fewer frames keep N evenly spaced frames with one pixel_patch call (the quick start shows it), never by lowering frames in the source, which stops the simulation early. A deterministic fluid simulation compiled into an ordinary recipe: one frame sequence and animation per effect (frames <effect>-0, <effect>-1…), each frame a palette grid operation, with obstacles stamped from symbols. Gases (smoke, fire, steam, explosions, magic) run stable fluids with buoyancy, vorticity confinement, dissipation and cooling; liquids (splashes, waterfalls, drips, potions) run FLIP particles on the same grid. Either may be viscous (honey, syrup, tar), and a liquid may have a yield stress (mud, slime). Look layers map fields onto palette ramps through ordered dither, so no colour outside the palette can appear. Looping effects warm up for whole cycles and blend their closing frames toward the frames before frame 0, so the last frame flows into the first. The same source gives the same recipe on every machine.

name.description: Portable name: do not use Windows device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–9, LPT1–9). Frame/animation names must be unique ignoring case.

width.description: Canvas width in pixels; the grid has one cell per pixel.

$ref.description: Shared palette file, resolved by the CLI and MCP relative to this recipe. Local entries add to or override it.

propertyNames.description: Portable name: do not use Windows device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–9, LPT1–9). Frame/animation names must be unique ignoring case.

symbols.description: Named rows for obstacles: braziers, logs, pipes, flasks, rocks.

anchor.description: Default pivot for every frame, exported to the atlas as anchor (exported pixels) and pivot (anchor / source size).

propertyNames.description: Portable name: do not use Windows device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–9, LPT1–9). Frame/animation names must be unique ignoring case.

kind.description: gas (default): smoke, fire, steam, explosions, magic. liquid: water, potions, honey and slime as FLIP particles.

duration.description: Milliseconds per frame, or one per frame; default 80.

loop.description: Seamless loop: emitter timing, pulses, orbits and noise repeat every cycle; the simulation warms up and its closing frames blend toward the frames before frame 0.

warmup.description: Loops: whole cycles simulated before the recorded one; default 2. Raise it when a flow takes long to settle (a filling pool).

blend.description: Loops: closing frames blended toward the previous cycle's; default a third of the frames, at most 8.

substeps.description: Simulation steps per frame; default 2. Raise for fast liquids; time grows with it (8 takes about twice as long as 4).

iterations.description: Pressure solve work per step, and with viscosity or yield as many steps of the viscosity solve; default 30 (gas) or 40 (liquid). A gas takes this many sweeps; a liquid a third as many conjugate-gradient steps, which settle long columns and channels.

buoyancy.description: Gas: upward acceleration per unit of temperature; default 0.15.

weight.description: Gas: downward acceleration per unit of density (negative floats smoke); default 0.

vorticity.description: Gas: vorticity confinement, which keeps small swirls so smoke curls; default 0.25.

dissipation.description: Gas: share of density lost per frame; default 0.03.

cooling.description: Gas: share of temperature lost per frame; default 0.08.

drag.description: Share of velocity lost per frame, as if the surroundings held the fluid back (water under water, a gas in still air); it slows falling too. For a thick fluid use viscosity. Default 0.02 (gas) or 0 (liquid).

advection.description: Gas: smooth (default) is plain semi-Lagrangian advection, which blurs a little every step; sharp (MacCormack with a limiter) keeps edges and small swirls crisp, at up to twice the cost; smoke lingers longer, so a one-shot may need more dissipation to end empty.

viscosity.description: Thickness, in square pixels per frame: it slows shearing and stretching but not falling or turning as a whole, so a thick drop falls as fast as water but spreads slowly and a stream never breaks into drops. Liquids: about 0.5 oil, 2–4 syrup, 8–16 honey, 32–64 tar. Gases: 0.1–1 for slow, smooth flows (a swirl dies away within frames above 1). Walls and obstacles hold a viscous fluid unless slip is set. Default 0.

yield.description: Liquid: yield stress, for mud, slime, dough and toothpaste. Below it the liquid is elastic and keeps its shape, squashing and springing back; pushed past it, it flows. A heap h pixels high holds itself up when yield is more than about gravity × h / 2. Default 0.

slip.description: With viscosity or yield: the fluid slides along walls and obstacles instead of being held by them (a greased pan). Default false.

flip.description: Liquid: FLIP share of each particle's velocity (lively, noisier) against the grid's (calm); default 0.9. A viscous liquid lowers it where it is thick.

apic.description: Liquid: affine particle-in-cell. The calm (grid) share of each particle's velocity also carries the turning and shearing of the flow around it, so calm and thick liquids keep their swirls and folds instead of smearing them. Use it with a low flip. Default false.

tension.description: Liquid: cohesion that keeps drops and streams together; default 0.5.

adhesion.description: Liquid: how strongly it holds on to walls and obstacles. Liquid touching a solid stays on it unless pulled away faster than about adhesion ÷ 2 pixels per frame, so a film clings under a ledge, to a spoon or down a jar's side, and moves with an obstacle that moves. An obstacle's own adhesion replaces it there. Default 0.

frame.description: The frame (within the cycle, for a loop) the change starts on.

over.description: Frames to move to the new values in a straight line; default 0, at once.

keys.description: Liquid: change yield, viscosity, adhesion, gravity or drag at a chosen frame, so the decisive moment lands where you want it: a heap held up by its yield gives way when a key drops it, a blob held under a ledge by adhesion drops when a key sets adhesion to 0, and drag (not viscosity, which freezes a slosh tilted) calms a one-shot so it ends at rest. Each setting starts from the effect's own value and follows the keys that name it, in frame order; a loop repeats them every cycle.

radius.description: Pixels from at, or [x, y] for an ellipse.

velocity.description: Starting velocity [x, y] in pixels per frame.

speed.description: How fast each piece flies out from the middle of the fill, in pixels per frame; [min, max] picks per piece.

burst.description: Break the fill into seeded pieces with a one-pixel gap between them and rounded corners, each flying straight out at its own speed (plus velocity): a liquid burst in mid-air. Outward velocity on one connected blob is cancelled by the pressure solve; separate pieces keep it. The water of the gaps and corners goes to their pieces, so the volume is kept.

temperature.description: With heat: the fill's temperature; default the air's (heat.ambient).

frozen.description: With heat: the fill starts as ice (an ice cube, a frozen pond); give it a temperature at or below heat.freeze.

vapour.description: With vapour: the fill holds still vapour of this density (1 a full cell of steam) instead of water: humid air for dew or frost.

fill.description: Liquid: water at frame 0 in discs or ellipses (at, radius), boxes (x, y, w, h) or their overlap (both): a disc cut by a box is a dome.

walls.description: Closed canvas edges. Open edges (the default) let gas and water out.

symbol.description: Portable name: do not use Windows device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–9, LPT1–9). Frame/animation names must be unique ignoring case.

x.description: Left edge; it may hang off the canvas by up to the symbol's width, and what hangs off is clipped.

y.description: Top edge; it may hang off the canvas by up to the symbol's height, and what hangs off is clipped.

draw.description: over (default): stamped in front of the fluid, its outline and sparks; under: behind its outline and sparks (the fluid itself never enters a solid obstacle); none: an invisible wall.

surface.description: pixels (default): the fluid meets every pixel step. smooth: it meets an outline traced through the steps, so a liquid slides down a drawn slope, roof or chute (a 1:1 staircase acts as a straight 45° slope; draw lines at least 2 pixels thick to smooth both sides), and a liquid can fall away from it instead of hanging on by suction (adhesion still holds it on). The obstacle is drawn as it is either way.

solid.description: false: a decoration, drawn over or under the fluid as draw says but never met by it (a net, a candle flame, a label, a background); with a voltage, an electrode the gas flows through (a cloud's charge, unseen with draw none). Default true.

over.description: Frames to move to it in a straight line; default 0, at once.

voltage.description: An electrode at this many volts, or keys that change it on cue (strikes, pulses); a loop repeats them. Arcs run between electrodes at different voltages, through a gas or the air over a liquid with heat and vapour.

resistance.description: The electrode supply's own resistance, so its voltage sags as current flows: a long arc starves, a shorter path takes over, and one strike stops the others. Default 0, an ideal supply.

charge.description: Charge the electrode stores (current × frames per volt), refilled through its resistance: strikes drain it and come in bursts. Default 0.

conductor.description: Metal at no set voltage, which arcs jump to and through (a gas, or a liquid with heat and vapour).

adhesion.description: Liquid: this obstacle's own adhesion, in place of the effect's, for liquid touching it: a sticky spoon (4) beside a non-stick pan (0).

temperature.description: A hot plate or a cold window: the obstacle keeps this temperature and warms or chills what touches it, a gas's air, or a liquid's water and ice and the air over them (the liquid needs heat). Obstacles without one take no part in the heat's flow.

frame.description: The frame (within the cycle, for a loop) the change starts on.

over.description: Frames to move to the new place in a straight line, in whole pixels; default 0, at once.

show.description: false takes the obstacle away (not drawn, not solid) from this frame on; true brings it back.

keys.description: Move the obstacle or take it away on cue: a dam that vanishes, a gate that lifts, a plunger, a paddle. Each key starts from where the obstacle is on its frame, and may take it partly or wholly off the canvas (up to its own size past an edge), where it is clipped: a rod reaching in, a load leaving. While a key's over runs, the obstacle pushes the fluid ahead of it (its faces carry its speed) and shoves fluid in cells it now covers to the first open cell, never through another solid; liquid flows in behind it, a viscous liquid is dragged along its sides, and with adhesion liquid touching it moves with it. A key with no over is a cut: the obstacle is simply elsewhere, pushes nothing, and fluid where it lands (or where an obstacle appears) is taken away. A loop repeats the keys every cycle.

obstacles.description: Solid shapes from symbols: their visible pixels block the flow (decorations with solid: false only draw). One may hang off the canvas by up to its own size; what hangs off is clipped, as the edge clips the fluid.

name.description: Portable name: do not use Windows device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–9, LPT1–9). Frame/animation names must be unique ignoring case.

at.description: Centre [x, y] in canvas pixels (one grid cell per pixel).

radius.description: A disc of this radius; default 2.

area.description: A box [w, h] centred on at, instead of a disc.

burst.description: Add the amounts once, at start (each cycle when looping), times this strength.

rate.description: Every frame from start until end, raise the covered cells toward the amounts times this strength, so a steady source holds its level.

start.description: Frame of the burst or first emission; default 0.

end.description: Frame where a rate emitter stops; default the last. A short window (end: 3) gives a burst that keeps growing for a few frames.

density.description: Gas: smoke added or held (default 0); negative drains. Liquid: share of each covered cell filled with water, 0–1 (default 1); negative drains that share of the particles there each frame.

temperature.description: Gas: heat added or held; heat rises by buoyancy and maps to fire ramps. Default 0. Liquid with heat: the temperature of the water it adds (default the air's, heat.ambient).

falloff.description: The amounts fall off from the centre toward the rim: 1 at the centre, 1 - falloff at the edge of the disc (or the ellipse inside the box), so a puff is densest in the middle. Default 0, a flat disc or box.

velocity.description: Flow [x, y] in pixels per frame: a rate emitter steers its cells toward it (a jet; [0, 0] holds them still, as a drop gathering at a tip), a burst adds it once.

expand.description: Push outward by this many pixels per frame while active (negative pulls inward): gas expands through the pressure solve, liquid particles are pushed.

vortex.description: Swirl speed around at, in pixels per frame; positive turns clockwise on screen.

noise.description: Random push in pixels per frame, coherent over about three pixels and new every frame (seeded): turbulence.

flicker.description: Random variation of strength from cell to cell and frame to frame (seeded value noise), so a flame base breaks into tongues.

amplitude.description: Share by which strength rises and falls; default 0.5. 1 switches the emitter off at the trough.

period.description: Frames per cycle; default the effect's frame count. A looping effect's period must divide its frame count.

phase.description: Degrees into the cycle at frame 0.

pulse.description: Strength follows a sine wave: puffs, heaves, heartbeats.

radius.description: Pixels from at, or [x, y] for an ellipse.

period.description: Frames per cycle; default the effect's frame count. A looping effect's period must divide its frame count. Negative turns anticlockwise; not 0.

phase.description: Degrees into the cycle at frame 0.

orbit.description: The emitter circles at (or follows an ellipse round it); a negative period turns anticlockwise. A rate emitter is laid along the path it covered since the last frame, so a fast orbit leaves a smooth trail.

drag.description: Share of the difference between a carrier's velocity and the air's that it loses each frame; default 0.1. Low throws dust far, high lets the air take it at once.

release.description: Share of what a carrier still holds that it hands to the air each frame; default 0.2. What it holds is drawn with the smoke.

gravity.description: Each carrier's own acceleration [x, y]; a small positive y lets dust settle. Default [0, 0].

carry.description: Gas: throw this emitter's smoke and heat (it needs a positive density or temperature) on heavy carriers, one per covered cell (each frame for a rate emitter, whose amounts are then thrown every frame; an orbiting one throws once a frame), launched with its velocity, vortex, expand (outward) and noise. A puff of gas cannot be thrown through still air, but dust can: carriers keep their momentum, slow by drag, hand their smoke to the air as they go and drop the rest where they meet an obstacle. For dust waves, skid smoke, dash trails.

count.description: Sparks per frame for a rate emitter (at most 16; fractions spawn on some frames), or in all for a burst; follows pulse and flicker.

life.description: Frames each spark lives; [min, max] picks per spark. Default [8, 16]. In a liquid, spray (follow 0) still in the air then flies on, for up to as long again, until it falls back in.

items.description: A one-character palette key (grid rows name colours by character).

colors.description: Palette keys spread over each spark's life, from birth to death.

size.description: Pixels across each spark; default 1. 2 reads at 1× (bubbles, embers, spray).

trail.description: Streak back to where the spark was a frame earlier, in the next colour of its list: flying debris, rising embers.

angle.description: Launch direction in degrees, clockwise: 0 right, 90 down, 270 up. Default [0, 360]. [min, max] picks per particle.

speed.description: Launch speed in pixels per frame; default 0. [min, max] picks per particle.

gravity.description: The spark's own acceleration [x, y]; negative y rises (bubbles, embers).

drag.description: Share of the spark's own speed lost each frame; default 0.05.

follow.description: How much the flow carries the spark: 1 (default) moves with the fluid, 0 ignores it (thrown debris). In a liquid, a spark with follow 0 that leaves the water ends where it falls back in (spray); one riding the flow out of the water flies on as a droplet, falling with the liquid's gravity unless it has its own, and ends the same way.

pop.description: Liquid only: the spark pops where it leaves the liquid, drawn as a ring around it for one frame and two droplets the next (bubbles bursting at the surface).

rise.description: Liquid: makes the spark a bubble that behaves like air. It rises this many pixels per frame through still water, against the liquid's gravity, on top of the flow that carries it (follow); it slides along any obstacle or closed edge it meets instead of ending there, up a sloping ceiling and out from under a ledge within 5 pixels, or waits under it, where waiting bubbles that touch merge into larger ones (up to 3 pixels across); it ends where it reaches the air, bursting there with pop. About 0.3–0.8.

wobble.description: With rise: pixels the bubble sways from side to side as it rises, once every eight frames from a seeded start. Default 0.

lift.description: With rise: share of its buoyancy the bubble hands to the water around it, as if that much of the water weighed nothing. A column of bubbles then drives an upwelling: 1 with about a bubble a frame raises a dome on the surface over it, 0.3 a slight bump. Default 0.

sparks.description: One-pixel particles carried by the flow and drawn over it: embers, sparkles, debris, bubbles. In a loop they wrap round, so they loop exactly.

emitters.description: 1–16 sources; a liquid with a fill, or a gas with electrodes, may have none (an empty list).

breakdown.description: Field, in volts per pixel, at which neutral gas breaks down; lower in hot gas. Default 3.

focus.description: How strongly growth favours the strongest field: about 1 forks freely like lightning, 3–4 runs on one path like an arc between close plates. Default 2.

growth.description: Cells of new plasma a frame, drawn one at a time where the field most exceeds breakdown (a leader's speed). Default 8.

recombine.description: Share of ionization lost a frame where no current holds it (slower in hot gas): the afterglow. Default 0.3.

sustain.description: Current that keeps a channel fully ionized; below half of it a channel goes out. Default 0.5.

memory.description: Frames a spent channel keeps guiding new strikes, which run down it at once (a restrike on the same channel). 0: none. Default 8.

heating.description: Temperature added a frame per unit of current squared (Joule heating), so buoyancy lifts an arc. Default 0.2.

ionize.description: Gas hotter than this is plasma too, fully at half as hot again: an arc's hot air, a fireball's core. Default 2, above every flame on the shared heat scale; 0 turns it off.

ground.description: Canvas edges held at 0 V, the world beyond: arcs that reach them strike them.

iterations.description: Conjugate-gradient steps of the field solve each step; default 24.

electric.description: Electricity and plasma. Obstacles with a voltage are electrodes; the field between them breaks the gas down into branching channels that conduct, glow, heat the gas and recombine. Defaults apply when only an obstacle has a voltage. A liquid with heat and vapour carries it too: arcs burn in the air over it (drawn by the vapour's look), land on the water, which conducts, and their current heats the water where they land, so it boils; ice hardly conducts.

field.description: density (smoke or water; water is 1 inside), temperature (gas heat; a liquid's water, ice or vapour with heat), speed (pixels per frame; foam, fast flow; a liquid has speed where there is water, a gas wherever its air moves, smoke or not), depth (pixels down from the liquid surface, 1 on the top row; from the third row down it follows the shallowest surface within three pixels along the row), light or shadow (0–1: how sharply density falls toward or away from the light; these only recolour pixels earlier layers drew), strand (liquids: 1 along a one-pixel path through liquid stretched thinner than the density can draw, a string joining two pieces or hanging at least 3 pixels off one, such as honey pulled up after a spoon), ionization (electric gases, and over a liquid in the vapour look: plasma, 0–1, 1 in a live channel, fading as it recombines) or current (electric gases and vapours: the current through each pixel; peak.current in the metadata gives the brightest).

items.description: A one-character palette key (grid rows name colours by character).

colors.description: Palette keys from the lowest level to the highest.

thresholds.description: One rising value per colour: each colour is fully on from its threshold up.

dither.description: Feather each colour in below its threshold through the pattern, over this share of the gap to the previous threshold (to 0 for the first). 0 draws hard bands; default 0.5.

pattern.description: Dither pattern, as for the dither operation: bayer4 (default), bayer2, bayer8, noise or value (seeded by the effect) or a matrix of ranks. Anchored to the canvas, so it never crawls.

color.description: A one-character palette key (grid rows name colours by character).

width.description: Pixels of glow; default 1 (the four neighbours).

halo.description: A glow of one colour on the empty pixels within width of what this layer drew: an arc's glow, a rim round a flame.

look.description: Layers drawn in order, later over earlier, each mapping one field to palette colours.

impact.description: Throw where a particle's velocity changes by at least this many pixels per frame within one frame: a drop landing, water striking water. Use impact or speed.

speed.description: Throw where a particle moves at least this many pixels per frame: a fast stream shedding drops. Use impact or speed.

chance.description: Share of qualifying surface particles that throw a droplet each frame (a seeded draw per particle); default 0.1.

throw.description: Droplet speed as a share of the impact or speed; default 1.

spread.description: Degrees of random turn either way; default 20.

life.description: Frames each droplet lives; [min, max] picks per droplet. Default [6, 12]. Spray still in the air then flies on, for up to as long again, until it falls back in.

items.description: A one-character palette key (grid rows name colours by character).

colors.description: Palette keys spread over each droplet's life, from birth to death.

trail.description: Streak back to where the droplet was a frame earlier, in the next colour of its list.

gravity.description: The droplet's own acceleration [x, y]; default the effect's gravity.

drag.description: Share of the droplet's speed lost each frame; default 0.02.

follow.description: How much the flow carries the droplet: 0 (default) is spray, drawn once it has left the water and ending where it falls back in; above 0 is foam carried on the flow, ending once it is carried under. Bubbles default to 1.

rise.description: Makes the layer bubbles instead of spray: air a plunging stream (speed) or a landing drop (impact) drives into a pool. They start under the surface, where water lies two pixels deep on every side, at rest in the water; they rise this many pixels per frame against the liquid's gravity, ride the flow, slide under obstacles and end at the surface, as sparks with rise do. throw, spread and gravity shape spray only.

wobble.description: Bubbles: pixels each sways from side to side as it rises, once every eight frames. Default 0.

lift.description: Bubbles: share of each one's buoyancy handed to the water around it (see the sparks' lift). Default 0.

pop.description: Bubbles: burst where they reach the surface, a ring for one frame and two droplets the next. Default false: they vanish there.

items.description: Spray and foam thrown off the liquid by its own motion, from particles at the surface, tipped away from the water; or, with rise, bubbles driven under it.

whitewater.description: Liquid: up to four layers of spray or foam thrown off the water where it lands or runs fast, drawn over it like sparks.

stiffness.description: Pixels of liquid head that squeeze a pocket to half its size: under h pixels of liquid a pocket keeps stiffness / (stiffness + h) of its size, and a pocket the liquid pulls on stretches the same way. Default 40; 1000 barely gives. Stable at any setting.

items.description: A one-character palette key (grid rows name colours by character).

colors.description: Palette keys spread over each bubble's life.

life.description: Frames each bubble lives; [min, max] picks per bubble. Default [30, 60].

rise.description: Pixels per frame each rises through still water; default 0.5.

wobble.description: Pixels each sways from side to side; default 0.

lift.description: Share of each one's buoyancy handed to the water; default 0.

pop.description: Burst where they reach the surface; default false.

bubbles.description: How the air of a pocket squeezed too small to show (under three cells) rises as bubbles, as large as the air it held, as sparks with rise do. Without it that air leaves unseen.

air.description: Liquid: air pockets that keep their air. Off by default, so sealed air collapses as the liquid fills it. With air, a region of air sealed off from the open canvas edges keeps its amount of air and pushes back by the gas law, so an upturned cup keeps most of its air, air stays under a shelf, a sealed bottle glugs as it pours and a big bubble rises. Bubbles gathering under a ceiling, two that touch with eight square pixels of air or more between them, become a pocket there, and a pocket that reaches open air vents. Every sealed space counts: a mould filling from above traps air in its tips, and a closed tank's air pushes on its water.

ambient.description: The room's air temperature, which air drifts back to; default 0. The scale is the gas one: water freezes at -0.5 and boils at 0.5, flames run about 0.3 to 1.

air.description: How fast the water's surface trades heat with the air, per frame; default 0.04.

conduct.description: How fast heat spreads through the water and ice, per frame; default 0.12.

contact.description: How fast a hot or cold obstacle (its temperature) warms or chills what touches it, per frame; default 0.15.

latent.description: Heat to melt or freeze, in degrees of the scale: the temperature holds at freeze while it is taken up or given off, so melting takes visible time and ice never flickers. Default 0.5.

vaporize.description: Heat to boil away, in degrees; each particle needs its own seeded half to one and a half of it, so a pot bubbles steadily. Default 1.

evaporation.description: With vapour: the chance each frame that a surface particle near the boil steams off (it falls off with the square of the temperature toward freeze): a warm puddle steams. Default 0.

dew.description: With vapour: vapour touching anything colder than this condenses, on a solid as dew (drawn as water) that drips off as a drop. Default boil - 0.1; at most boil.

condense.description: Share of such vapour that condenses each frame; default 0.2.

frost.description: With vapour: vapour touching ice or an obstacle colder than this grows straight into ice (frost) as fern-like fingers, only from cold surfaces (corners first) and frost already there, and only into air below freeze. Off unless set; at most freeze.

deposit.description: Share of such vapour that turns to frost each frame, at a finger's tip; default 0.1.

branch.description: With vapour: how often a frost finger forks at 45 degrees into a shorter branch, at every other cell along it; 0 grows straight fingers. Default 0.5.

sublimate.description: With vapour: ice turns straight into vapour at its surface instead of melting (dry ice). Default false.

grain.description: Seeded unevenness in where water freezes and frost grows, so fronts are ragged. Default 0.

heat.description: Liquid: phase changes. Each particle carries heat; water below freeze turns to ice where it touches ice or a cold solid (or 0.5 below freeze anywhere), ice holds still or settles as a piece and floats, and a cell of ice is solid to the flow, to bubbles and to air pockets. With vapour, water boils into steam, and steam condenses or frosts back. Water, ice and vapour are counted every frame in the figures (water, ice, vapour, added, taken). Obstacles may move on keys or be smooth: a hot spoon, a heated piston or a smooth hot plate work as a still one does.

expansion.description: Cells a cell's worth of water fills as vapour: how much room steam takes on screen and how hard boiling pushes the air. Default 8.

buoyancy.description: Lift per degree above the air's temperature, against gravity; default 0.2.

weight.description: Sinking per unit of vapour density (negative lifts it: steam is light, dry-ice fog heavy); default 0.

dissipation.description: Share of vapour that fades each frame (it leaves the figures as taken); default 0.

cooling.description: Share of the air's difference from heat.ambient lost each frame; default 0.05.

spread.description: Diffusion between neighbouring cells per step, which keeps matter; for still humid air that feeds frost. Default 0.

items.description: A one-character palette key (grid rows name colours by character).

colors.description: Palette keys spread over each bubble's life.

lift.description: Share of its buoyancy handed to the water, so a boil churns the pot.

bubbles.description: Bubbles a boil makes inside the water, as sparks with rise: they carry their vapour up and let it out at the surface (into an air pocket, they add to its air). Without them water boils only at its surface.

field.description: density (smoke or water; water is 1 inside), temperature (gas heat; a liquid's water, ice or vapour with heat), speed (pixels per frame; foam, fast flow; a liquid has speed where there is water, a gas wherever its air moves, smoke or not), depth (pixels down from the liquid surface, 1 on the top row; from the third row down it follows the shallowest surface within three pixels along the row), light or shadow (0–1: how sharply density falls toward or away from the light; these only recolour pixels earlier layers drew), strand (liquids: 1 along a one-pixel path through liquid stretched thinner than the density can draw, a string joining two pieces or hanging at least 3 pixels off one, such as honey pulled up after a spoon), ionization (electric gases, and over a liquid in the vapour look: plasma, 0–1, 1 in a live channel, fading as it recombines) or current (electric gases and vapours: the current through each pixel; peak.current in the metadata gives the brightest).

thresholds.description: One rising value per colour: each colour is fully on from its threshold up.

dither.description: Feather each colour in below its threshold through the pattern, over this share of the gap to the previous threshold (to 0 for the first). 0 draws hard bands; default 0.5.

pattern.description: Dither pattern, as for the dither operation: bayer4 (default), bayer2, bayer8, noise or value (seeded by the effect) or a matrix of ranks. Anchored to the canvas, so it never crawls.

width.description: Pixels of glow; default 1 (the four neighbours).

halo.description: A glow of one colour on the empty pixels within width of what this layer drew: an arc's glow, a rim round a flame.

look.description: Gas-style layers for the vapour (density 1 is a cell full of steam, temperature, speed, light, shadow), drawn under the water. Without them vapour is invisible.

vapour.description: Liquid with heat: steam and fog, moved by the gas solver through the cells holding neither water nor ice; the water and ice are walls moving with it.

field.description: density (smoke or water; water is 1 inside), temperature (gas heat; a liquid's water, ice or vapour with heat), speed (pixels per frame; foam, fast flow; a liquid has speed where there is water, a gas wherever its air moves, smoke or not), depth (pixels down from the liquid surface, 1 on the top row; from the third row down it follows the shallowest surface within three pixels along the row), light or shadow (0–1: how sharply density falls toward or away from the light; these only recolour pixels earlier layers drew), strand (liquids: 1 along a one-pixel path through liquid stretched thinner than the density can draw, a string joining two pieces or hanging at least 3 pixels off one, such as honey pulled up after a spoon), ionization (electric gases, and over a liquid in the vapour look: plasma, 0–1, 1 in a live channel, fading as it recombines) or current (electric gases and vapours: the current through each pixel; peak.current in the metadata gives the brightest).

items.description: A one-character palette key (grid rows name colours by character).

colors.description: Palette keys from the lowest level to the highest.

thresholds.description: One rising value per colour: each colour is fully on from its threshold up.

dither.description: Feather each colour in below its threshold through the pattern, over this share of the gap to the previous threshold (to 0 for the first). 0 draws hard bands; default 0.5.

pattern.description: Dither pattern, as for the dither operation: bayer4 (default), bayer2, bayer8, noise or value (seeded by the effect) or a matrix of ranks. Anchored to the canvas, so it never crawls.

color.description: A one-character palette key (grid rows name colours by character).

width.description: Pixels of glow; default 1 (the four neighbours).

halo.description: A glow of one colour on the empty pixels within width of what this layer drew: an arc's glow, a rim round a flame.

look.description: Gas-style layers for the ice, drawn cell by cell over the water (density 0.5 is a cell of ice).

ice.description: Liquid with heat: how ice is drawn; default the water's look.

light.description: Direction toward the light for the light and shadow fields; default [-1, -1], the upper left.

outline.description: Palette key for a one-pixel outline around the fluid.

cleanup.description: De-Stray (specks and pinholes take their surroundings' colour; a liquid's lone pixel is a drop, and stays) and De-Corner cleanup of the fluid before outline and sparks.

trim.description: Pack each frame by its visible bounds; the atlas reports trimmed rectangles with spriteSourceSize. Ignores columns.

rows.description: Equal-width text rows. Every character is a palette key; dot and space skip a pixel.
